Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go! September 3, 2026 – 6:04 AMHello and welcome to live coverage of stage 12 of the Vuelta a España!September 3, 2026 – 6:32 AMBasically, LOTS of climbing. 4,475m of elevation gain and 62.2km of categorised climbing, to be precise. September 3, 2026 – 6:33 AMOne abandon to report already this morning: Ben Tulett won't be starting.He crashed a few days ago so will head home. The British climber hasn't really had the Vuelta he might have hoped for, but Visma-Lease a Bike still have former winner Sepp Kuss in the GC conversation.September 3, 2026 – 6:36 AMSpeaking of crashes, here's the latest update on Pogačar after he crashed out of the race last Saturday.Tadej Pogačar out of hospital after Vuelta a España crash and injuries but questions remain regarding World ChampionshipsSlovenian set to recover at home from injuries, date on return yet to be announcedSeptember 3, 2026 – 6:41 AMIt's back to the GC action after what was a fairly tame sprint day yesterday. If you missed out on any of that stage, here's the report and results.Vuelta a España: Matthew Brennan nets hat-trick with victory on stage 11 using lead-out by Wout van AertBryan Coquard and Jordi Meeus earn podium spots in LorcaSeptember 3, 2026 – 6:44 AMThe riders will start in just over 15 minutes, with a short neutral and the official start slated for 13:07 local time.They'll be climbing almost straight away, with the official start of the Alto del Cabecico coming 8km into the stage.September 3, 2026 – 6:46 AMLooks like Ethan Hayter won a trophy and a prize of bananas at the start this morning. I wish I could tell you what that was for...September 3, 2026 – 6:47 AMOh, Hayter's prize is for the most combative rider on stage 11.How did I not know until today that the prize for that is bananas?!September 3, 2026 – 6:49 AMIt's about 32° C at the start today, so riders are trying to keep cool. We've really had every type of weather in this Vuelta. Remember the hail storm?September 3, 2026 – 6:57 AMPrimož Roglič just gave the most Primož Roglič interview to the host broadcasters.They asked him if he would prefer if today was a breakaway.Uhhh, yeah... I don't care, eh? It will be hard anyway.September 3, 2026 – 7:03 AMThe peloton have just rolled away from the start line for a short neutral section.September 3, 2026 – 7:06 AMA couple of other riders didn't start today, alongside Tulett:Lindsay De Vylder (Alpecin-Premier Tech)David González (Pinarello Q36.5)September 3, 2026 – 7:10 AM166.6km and over 60km of uphill to come. September 3, 2026 – 7:11 AMFuelled by his bananas, Ethan Hayter is the first rider to try to attack as the break formation begins.September 3, 2026 – 7:13 AMEF Education-EasyPost are throwing plenty of riders into the mix here. Them, Tudor, Uno-X all clearly want to be in the break. September 3, 2026 – 7:17 AMSmall crash in the bunch, Fredrik Wahndal (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) went down but was back up and riding quickly. Tense in the peloton though.September 3, 2026 – 7:18 AMNo break yet, but we're only 6km in.September 3, 2026 – 7:21 AMStart of the climb. It's long-ish but a pretty gentle gradient. It's steeper near the top.September 3, 2026 – 7:23 AMWout van Aert is getting involved now. He's after green jersey points mainly, but he's also close enough to the lead of the mountains jersey that that could be of interest to him too...He's not going to win that jersey but it would be nice to wear it.September 3, 2026 – 7:26 AMJay Vine gave a kind of avoidant interview to Eurosport. Saying he's not feeling good, but he doesn't know why. He didn't want to say much.September 3, 2026 – 7:29 AMVine is struggling at the back, whilst his teammate Oliveira is off the front with a couple of riders. Still not an established break as we approach the top of the climb.September 3, 2026 – 7:31 AMPlenty of riders have been in the action today.September 3, 2026 – 7:32 AMGregor Muhlberger (Decathlon CMA CGM) stopped and got off his bike, and also started taking his shoe off. Not sure if he's needing a bike change or a shoe change...September 3, 2026 – 7:32 AMUp front, Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) is leading the way in trying to get into the break, but nothing is sticking yet.September 3, 2026 – 7:34 AMWout van Aert wins maximum points with a little sprint over the top.September 3, 2026 – 7:34 AMVan Aert and Buitrago have just chipped off the front of the peloton with that KOM effort.September 3, 2026 – 7:38 AM20km done, Van Aert and Buitrago are reeled in. The breakaway battle starts anew.September 3, 2026 – 7:39 AMVan Aert isn't having a bad Vuelta, but his own team admitted that he does need to win for himself at some point. Today is probably too hard, but it's still good to see him in the mix.Return to lead-out duties for Wout van Aert brings Visma more success at Vuelta a España, but he also needs wins himself says DS'Hopefully he will win one stage, but on the other hand, he is an excellent teammate, and he wants to help Matthew Brennan win more stages' says Frans MaassenSeptember 3, 2026 – 7:41 AMA new move has a pretty decent gap.Alexey Lutsenko (NSN), Axel Laurance (Netcompany Ineos) and Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech).September 3, 2026 – 7:41 AMYoung Aussie Hamish McKenzie (Jayco AlUla) has quit after crashing yesterday.September 3, 2026 – 7:42 AMThe three leaders have a bigger gap that anyone has had today, but I'm not sure three is a big enough break for today. I would say too many teams will be chasing behind for this to be able to stick.September 3, 2026 – 7:49 AMWe've got just over 20km of rolling road now before the next categorised climb.Various riders are trying to chase across to our three leaders.September 3, 2026 – 7:55 AMOscar Onley looks to have come off heavily round a roundabout, his white jersey is covered in dirt from the road. He's remounted his bike and he's chasing back on.Luke Tuckwell also went down, and a rider from Picnic PostNL.September 3, 2026 – 7:55 AMNo teammates with Onley just yet. He's just drafting behind the Ineos car.September 3, 2026 – 7:56 AMOof just saw the replay of the crash. Onley just slid out on the exit of the roundabout, landing on a patch of grass outside a Lidl. Looked heavy by the grass will have softened the blow.September 3, 2026 – 7:57 AMThe Scot got a nice word of encouragement and a push from his former Picnic teammate Timo Roosen.September 3, 2026 – 7:58 AMOnley and fellow chasers are a minute down on the peloton because the bunch are going at full pelt now. They'll be able to get back on but it's not ideal.September 3, 2026 – 7:59 AMAmazing landscapes in Andalucía.September 3, 2026 – 8:00 AMBack to the front of the race, our three leaders have just been joined by a large group of chasers – over 20 of them. Big group at the front now.September 3, 2026 – 8:00 AMThe gap is still small. Teams will have to asses who has made it and who hasn't before they decide if this big move is going to be allowed to go.September 3, 2026 – 8:02 AMVan Aert is in this 27-rider front group. But I think they're about to be caught and the situation will reset once again...September 3, 2026 – 8:06 AMSeems I spoke prematurely – the peloton is slowing up so I think this break of 27 will be our move of the day.I'll list the full names when we have them.September 3, 2026 – 8:06 AMOscar Onley is back in the peloton, so Ineos can relax briefly now.September 3, 2026 – 8:07 AMThe peloton are going almost comically slow now, letting the gap go out to a minute.September 3, 2026 – 8:08 AMSome riders in this break don't seem to want to be in such a big group. A few of them are trying to get away in a smaller break.September 3, 2026 – 8:09 AMOscar Onley is visiting the medical car.Check the widget above for a list of names in the break.September 3, 2026 – 8:12 AMHere's the names in the break:September 3, 2026 – 8:13 AMThe biggest GC threat in the group is Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) who sits at 8:05 down on Enric Mas, so Movistar will have to keep this somewhat controlled.The gap is approaching three minutes currently. September 3, 2026 – 8:13 AMPretty impressive to see Tuckwell in this break after crashing today. He crashed last weekend too.September 3, 2026 – 8:20 AMMovistar are on the front of the bunch.September 3, 2026 – 8:22 AMThere is a chasing group in between the peloton and the break – it's made up of Pavel Sivakov (UAE Team Emirates-XRG), Chris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL) and José Manuel Díaz (Burgos Burpellet BH). They're about a minute behind the break.September 3, 2026 – 8:26 AMDíaz and Hamilton have joined the break. Sivakov hasn't made it. Should be 30 riders in the lead now.September 3, 2026 – 8:27 AMCorrection, Sivakov has made it, so 31 in the lead. Tracker is showing him as behind but we can see he is in the break.September 3, 2026 – 8:30 AMVan Aert wins maximum points again. He really is keen to go after this jersey, but he's only made up 2 points in his 11-point deficit to Buitrago.September 3, 2026 – 8:32 AMHere's a look at Wout van Aert in the break.Who do you think will win today? Break or peloton? Let me know in the comments.September 3, 2026 – 8:33 AMImages of Onley's crash, in case you missed it.September 3, 2026 – 8:35 AMSivakov confusion again. It was not him that we could see joining the break... He's actually given up and waited for the peloton. September 3, 2026 – 8:40 AMThe gap has just reached five minutes.September 3, 2026 – 8:43 AMBuitrago is pushing on in the front of the break, trying to whittle things down a bit.Riders like him will be hoping they can get rid of Omrzel, because that will give a smaller break a better chance of winning the stage.Van Aert, Almeida, Lutsenko, Bisiaux and Kron are with him.September 3, 2026 – 8:44 AMStill a lot of action and climbing to come today.September 3, 2026 – 8:48 AMThat early attempt to split up the break hasn't really worked, still a big group all together at the base of this long climb.September 3, 2026 – 8:50 AMBahrain are understandably taking a lot of responsibility in the break. They have KOM points and GC positions to gain.September 3, 2026 – 8:51 AMIf you're looking for something to read whilst the race is relatively calm, I spoke with Paul Seixas yesterday about his upcoming races.Paul Seixas raring to take on Canadian GPs and World Championships with Pogačar possible absence opening up opportunitiesFrench star will return from post-Tour de France break at Grand Prix Québec before big goals of Worlds and Il LombardiaSeptember 3, 2026 – 9:02 AMStill 11km left of this climb to go. It hasn't been too eventful so far.September 3, 2026 – 9:05 AMIt's deceptively calm right now. Still two really big climbs to come after this one.September 3, 2026 – 9:11 AMThe gap is up to six minutes now. How much elastic are the peloton going to give this break? At what point does it come un-closeable?With two such long climbs left, a lot can change in the finale, so six minutes definitely isn't too much to close, but I wonder what Movistar's strategy is here.September 3, 2026 – 9:20 AMWoooops Luke Tuckwell nearly crashed into a soigneur in the feed zone there. Just about avoided disaster.September 3, 2026 – 9:25 AMVan Aert and Buitrago go head to head for the points and WVA wins it again.September 3, 2026 – 9:26 AMVan Aert has 30 points in the KOM classification now, and Buitrago has 38.September 3, 2026 – 9:27 AMVan Aert and Buitrago are on their own on the descent again, just pushing on after that KOM sprint. September 3, 2026 – 9:31 AMVan Aert and Buitrago have 20 seconds on the rest of the break, and 6:40 on the peloton.September 3, 2026 – 9:32 AMEnjoying our live race coverage? Subscribe to Cyclingnews for an all-access pass to our unrivalled reporting of WorldTour racing, bike tech and exclusive in-depth features. Plus, access to the Cyclingnews app to follow the action on-the-go!September 3, 2026 – 9:33 AMI think Van Aert and Buitrago have just agreed to slow up and wait for the rest of the break to rejoin them.September 3, 2026 – 9:34 AMOur leaders have been swept back up by the break.September 3, 2026 – 9:42 AMGap is coming down ever so slightly. The road will head uphill soon, though the Alto del Velefique doesn't officially start for another 15km.September 3, 2026 – 9:46 AMThe break aren't really working that well together anymore. Some riders are committed and taking their turns but others are not quite sharing the load. September 3, 2026 – 9:47 AMElsewhere in the cycling world, stage 2 of the Tour of Britain Men just finished.September 3, 2026 – 9:49 AMMas is looking comfortable but alert in the red jersey in the peloton.September 3, 2026 – 9:52 AMThe gap is nearly seven minutes now. Still 30 riders in the front – no one has really been dropped.Movistar are riding at their own pace on the front of the bunch, not really chasing.September 3, 2026 – 9:57 AMJakob Omrzel is getting pretty close to the virtual lead now.Movistar don't seem to care that much right now – they can be confident that the gap own't be eight minutes at the end of the day – but they might think they can lure other teams into doing some work.September 3, 2026 – 10:07 AMStarting the penultimate, cat. 1 climb. There's bonus seconds at the top of this one, and the intermediate sprint is in a few kilometres.September 3, 2026 – 10:10 AMAlmeida and UAE are setting a pace here which is finally putting some riders in trouble and beginning to make the selections in this group.No trouble for Van Aert though, who takes 20 pts at the sprint.September 3, 2026 – 10:11 AMVan Aert has sat up and is now going backwards fast. Mission accomplished for him, extending his lead in green and grabbing some bonus KOM points.September 3, 2026 – 10:13 AMAlmeida is still grinding away on the front. Does this mean he's working for Vermaerke instead of himself, or is he just the strongest rider in this group?September 3, 2026 – 10:17 AMAular pulls out of the Movistar line-out, so there's just Mas and one teammate left on the front of the peloton.September 3, 2026 – 10:18 AMHe's just shedding riders behind him. Really strong ride on this climb. Vermaerke is on his wheel.September 3, 2026 – 10:20 AM8.8km left of this climb, and then there's the 17km Calar Alto still to come.At present, Omrzel is in virtual second, behind only Mas...September 3, 2026 – 10:22 AMNice shot of Van Aert and Buitrago from earlier.September 3, 2026 – 10:22 AMAlmeida has pulled off and gone out the back of the break.September 3, 2026 – 10:23 AMDespite Movistar's depleted numbers, they've clearly been riding hard on the front of the bunch as they've been really whittling down the GC group, lots of riders going out the back.They haven't made too big of a dent in the gap, though, because of Almeida's huge effort.September 3, 2026 – 10:24 AMBilbao and Buitrago are pushing on at the front of the break.September 3, 2026 – 10:25 AMBilbao's efforts have pulled out a small group: Buitrago, Lutsenko, Bisiaux, Verkmaerke, Haig, Berrade and Tuckwell.September 3, 2026 – 10:28 AMIván Romeo is putting in a serious pull in the peloton. Lots of riders struggling to live with the pace.Once Romeo is done, Mas will be alone in that group, but he has teammates up the road that he can reunite with. September 3, 2026 – 10:30 AMCarapaz attacks 5km from the topFewer than 20 riders in the GC group.Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) launches a big attack!September 3, 2026 – 10:31 AMBig bold attack from Carapaz, he went speeding out of the group.September 3, 2026 – 10:32 AMCarapaz is speeding past dropped break riders – Ivo Oliveira even handed him a bottle – and he's 30 seconds ahead of Mas and co.September 3, 2026 – 10:34 AMThere's been a regrouping up front, 15 riders in the lead just now.September 3, 2026 – 10:35 AMEvidence of that monster effort from Almeida.September 3, 2026 – 10:36 AMOmrzel has just chipped off the front of the break, with Bisiaux on his wheel. These are the two best-placed GC riders in the break.September 3, 2026 – 10:36 AMI think Omrzel is riding for his own interests, but for Bisiaux, his role is more about being a satellite rider for Felix Gall.September 3, 2026 – 10:38 AMCarapaz is still on his mission behind, but it feels a bit futile.He's five minutes behind the break and only 22ish in front of the peloton.September 3, 2026 – 10:38 AMBisiaux declines to work with Omrzel.September 3, 2026 – 10:41 AMOmrzel and Bisiaux have 17 seconds on the next group, but only the Slovenian is working.September 3, 2026 – 10:42 AMCarapaz is caught by the GC group after a big pull from Romeo.September 3, 2026 – 10:42 AMEnjoying our live race coverage? Subscribe to Cyclingnews for an all-access pass to our unrivalled reporting of WorldTour racing, bike tech and exclusive in-depth features. Plus, access to the Cyclingnews app to follow the action on-the-go!September 3, 2026 – 10:43 AMOmrzel and Bisiaux caught. Nearly at the top now so Buitrago is winding up to score some more points.September 3, 2026 – 10:44 AMBuitrago graps the maximum 10 points, just ahead of Lutsenko.September 3, 2026 – 10:45 AMThe GC group catches up with Castrillo from the break, so Romeo can finally pull off. Mega ride from him.September 3, 2026 – 10:49 AMThe peloton just crested the top of the climb.September 3, 2026 – 10:55 AMStill descending, but the road will kick up again soon for the Calar Alto.September 3, 2026 – 10:57 AMEF Education-EasyPost are amassed behind Movistar in the GC group. Carapaz must be feeling good to try something again today.September 3, 2026 – 11:01 AMOnto the final climb we go!The first section is the steepest part.September 3, 2026 – 11:04 AMRomeo is back on the front in the GC group. What a machine.September 3, 2026 – 11:05 AMLuke Tuckwell and Jack Haig are getting dropped from the lead group. Lutsenko too.September 3, 2026 – 11:07 AMThe gap is still five minutes.Buitrago is pushing the pace in the lead. Berrade is sticking with him really well, with Bisiaux and Omrzel behind.September 3, 2026 – 11:08 AMThe French squad are winding up the pace on the front of the GC group now as they hit the hardest part of the climb.It's already making life difficult for Skjelmose and Kuss.September 3, 2026 – 11:09 AMDecathlon are riding for Giro runner-up Felix Gall, who is 1:39 behind Mas overall.September 3, 2026 – 11:10 AMCallum Scotson is setting the pace, with Riccitello and Muhlberger still there behind him so Gall has plenty of support.But as I say that, Riccitello pulls off, he can't stay with his own team. So suddenly Gall only has Muhlberger with him.September 3, 2026 – 11:11 AMIt's only Muhlberger, Gall, Mas, Onley, Roglič and Carapaz in the GC group now.They're still 4:35 down on the leaders with 13km to go, so it might not be a fight for the stage, but we'll see some GC action today.September 3, 2026 – 11:12 AMMas and Roglič are able to follow, Onley can't.September 3, 2026 – 11:13 AMUp front, Omrzel and Berrade are dropping Bisiaux after Buitrago pulled off.September 3, 2026 – 11:13 AMGall is trying to get Mas to come through for a turn. Obviously he doesn't.September 3, 2026 – 11:14 AMThe gap is coming down pretty rapidly, actually, and still 12km to go. Stage win still open.September 3, 2026 – 11:17 AMHe dispatches with Berrade and leads by himself.He's riding for both a stage win and a big GC gain, both of which would be massive for the 20-year-old Slovenian.September 3, 2026 – 11:18 AMThe gap is hovering at four minutes now after initially falling.September 3, 2026 – 11:19 AMBig move from the red jersey, riding away from Roglič and Gall quickly with apparent ease. Neither had anything in response.He has a chance to really extend and solidify his GC lead here. September 3, 2026 – 11:20 AMOmrzel has 1:15 on Berrade, 3:50 on Mas.Can he hold off the red jersey to take the stage win?September 3, 2026 – 11:21 AMSeptember 3, 2026 – 11:23 AMMas catches up with García Pierna from the break, and hops onto his wheel for some help.September 3, 2026 – 11:26 AMIt's Gall who is doing all the work in the chase group, Roglič isn't really contributing.September 3, 2026 – 11:29 AMTuckwell joins Roglič in the chase. Bisiaux also comes back. So now there's a bit of an actual chase to be had.September 3, 2026 – 11:30 AMMas (with García Pierna) has just under 45 seconds on Gall and Roglič.With Tuckwell and Bisiaux there now, can he hold them off?September 3, 2026 – 11:30 AMOmrzel is on the way to victoryGarcía Pierna drops away, and Mas is still 3:40 down on Omrzel.He won't make that up in 4km – the Slovenian is going to win the stage, bar disaster.September 3, 2026 – 11:32 AMTuckwell, Bisiaux and Muhlberger are all there in the chase group as domestiques, and they are making gains on Mas.September 3, 2026 – 11:33 AMIt's steep again up the top. Omrzel looks so tired, but he's so close to such a special win.September 3, 2026 – 11:35 AMWho needs Pogačar? The Vuelta has a new Slovenian star today.Omrzel leads by 3:22 over Mas. There are remnants of the break in between the two, so Mas is't riding for second place currently.September 3, 2026 – 11:36 AMMas is holding firm with a 40 second gap, the chasers' advancements have definitely stalled.September 3, 2026 – 11:37 AMIt's bare and exposed on the top of this climb. Really atmospheric and plenty of fans have made their way up.The chasers can see Mas on these long, straight final kilometres.September 3, 2026 – 11:38 AMOmrzel is bringing it home!Muhlberger is doing the work chasing Mas, but they're not making many inroads.September 3, 2026 – 11:39 AMJakob Omrzel wins stage 12!What a HUGE result for the 20-year-old, well-earnt after a whole day in the breakaway, riding everyone off his wheel and indeed holding off none other than the race leader.We'll have to wait to see just what gains he's made in the GC.September 3, 2026 – 11:41 AMIt's not quite clear how many riders were in between Omrzel and Mas, so not sure yet if the Spaniard will take bonus points here.September 3, 2026 – 11:42 AMUrko Berrade takes second, Santiago Buitrago thirdThat's a fantastic result for Kern Pharma. And a 1-3 for Bahrain.No bonus points for Mas, but he's still gaining a lot.September 3, 2026 – 11:43 AMSeptember 3, 2026 – 11:43 AMLooks like Mas finished about 30 seconds ahead of Gall and Roglič to add to his GC lead.September 3, 2026 – 11:46 AMOnley just finished the stage, a good two minutes down on Mas.September 3, 2026 – 11:47 AMJakob Omrzel (Slo) Bahrain VictoriousUrko Berrade Fernandez (Spa) Kern PharmaSantiago Buitrago (Col) Bahrain VictoriousAlexey Lutsenko (Kaz) NSN CyclingMauri Vansevenant (Bel) Soudal Quick-StepFélix Gall (Aut) Decathlon CMA CGMPrimoz Roglic (Slo) Red Bull-Bora-HansgroheRichard Carapaz (Ecu) EF Education-EasyPostGregor Mühlberger (Aut) Decathlon CMA CGMSeptember 3, 2026 – 11:48 AMA really solid day out for Mas.September 3, 2026 – 11:49 AMLove the confidence from Omrzel at the finish.I'm not surprised, because I know how much work I put in, and I knew that this day was going to come sooner or later. But for sure I was not expecting it 100% in the first Grand Tour. I still can't believe what I did, but I felt super good, I'm still feeling OK, I'm not tired. So I'm just enjoying it at the moment.September 3, 2026 – 11:52 AMPrimoz Roglic (Slo) Red Bull-Bora-HansgroheFélix Gall (Aut) Decathlon CMA CGMRichard Carapaz (Ecu) EF Education-EasyPostOscar Onley (GBr) Netcompany IneosJakob Omrzel (Slo) Bahrain VictoriousMattias Skjelmose (Den) Lidl-TrekSepp Kuss (USA) Visma-Lease A BikeGregor Mühlberger (Aut) Decathlon CMA CGMHarold Tejada (Col) XDS AstanaSeptember 3, 2026 – 12:04 PMCatch up with the full stage report here.Vuelta a España: Jakob Omrzel wins stage 12 as Enric Mas has another stellar ride on Calar AltoMovistar rider extends his race lead on searing daySeptember 3, 2026 – 12:08 PMMore on Onley's tough day today.Oscar Onley suffers huge dent to Vuelta a España podium hopes after early crash and summit finish strugglesNetcompany Ineos leader drops from fourth to fifth on a trying day

item.title: 'We are still careful in speaking this out' – Primož Roglič in position to strike and win fifth Vuelta a España, say Red Bull, but pre-race crash keeps them realistic
item.content:encoded: No one knows how to close out the Vuelta a España better than four-time winner Primož Roglič (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), except perhaps for Roberto Heras, the man with whom he shares the record for the most red jersey overall titles.However, after the abandon of Tadej Pogačar on stage 8, Roglič now has the chance to win that elusive fifth, an outcome which he and his team didn't think possible before the start, the Slovenian having been hit by a driver in the build-up to the Spanish Grand Tour. And while he doesn't have the lead for the moment with 10 stages left to race, his long-term Vuelta rival Enric Mas (Movistar) has that honour; Roglič is only 1:18 down, and with a final week time trial playing into his hands. But he likely has to impress on all the remaining mountain stages too if he is to win this Vuelta, the next of which comes today to Calar Alto, with an irregular 17km climb that averages 5.6% gradient set to bring the GC stars back into focus. "I'm happy, huh. I'm happy I'm still here. I hope I stay with already some hard days in the legs, tired, but happy," said Roglič at the start of stage 11 in Cartagena. "We will see. At the end, I'm not the only one, it's a lot of strong guys, and for the moment, Enric was the best one; he won last time. There's a long way still to go; we just have to do our best and see what happens."That pre-race crash which almost saw him not to take the start is what's left Roglič as such an unknown quantity at this Vuelta. Yes, he has looked strong so far, but having missed important days of training, will he be able to maintain it for three weeks?"I still feel it, I still feel my leg when I touch the area," he said, gesturing to the spot where he was struck in training near Livigno."I'm happy; I didn't expect to be in the place I am, so we just have to see how I will react to all of these efforts."'He missed 10 important days, and we still have 10 days to go'And for his team, while they note how they are in a position where winning this Vuelta is very much possible, they are cautious about being overly bullish given how much the crash could come to affect him as the fatigue wears on. "The question mark was before the Vuelta, and I think this was from Primož's side and from our side, but we always had the goal to still believe in a good GC result," said Red Bull sports director Sven Vanthourenhout to on Wednesday. "So it's not that we didn't expect anything anymore from him. The GC with Primož was still one of the most important goals. Of course, especially with Pogi on the start, we knew it should be difficult to win the Vuelta. Even a podium with the preparation he had before the Vuelta was doubtful, but now we are in a nice second place. "We are still careful because we always say we know what happened before the Vuelta. He missed 10 important days, and we still have 10 days to go. So we stay careful. We know what's coming. We know that it's still a hard last week that we have to manage. "In a normal way, without a crash, then we also believe that he can grow even 1% or 2% and that he's a really big contender to win the Vuelta. Yes, it is possible. We are in a spot that we can win the Vuelta, but we are still careful in speaking this out."Before the remaining time trial of this year's Vuelta, a mostly flat 32km race against the clock to Jerez on stage 18, Roglič will want to get through today's stage and Saturday's brutal climbing test to Sierra de la Pandera (11.8km at 7.5%) still within striking distance of Mas' lead.Roglič has never lost to Mas in a time trial, so he can be almost certain of gaining time that day, but his recent form in TTs has not been world-beating as it was between 2018 and 2022. Red Bull are certainly eyeing it up as the potential perfect place to hit out for red. "For us, he's still the much better TT rider than Mas and Gall," said Vanthourenhout. "Now in the second, in the third week, he will also be cooling down on his TT bike; these are not big secrets. That means that he's focused and that he still believes in it."The Belgian DS again caveated this confidence by saying how Roglič could still come unstuck – him getting gradually better as he did in Vueltas gone by isn't as guaranteed. It's fair to say they won't be leaving any stone unturned in pursuit of red, though."After the Vuelta, we want to look back and say, OK, we did what we could, we did all that we had to do, and we took the maximum out of this Vuelta," he said."It will be an interesting week, and it is possible that Primož is coming closer. It's also possible that he will lose some time somewhere. We have to see what will happen. But anyway, we are there for him, and we will see what it will bring."Expecting attacks on stage 12Vanthourenhout is expecting third-place Felix Gall's Decathlon CMA CGM team to take control once again on stage 12, with the Austrian needing to make up time on both Mas and Roglič. He's put his strong team to work several times, notably destroying the peloton on stage 9 up the Alto de Aitana, but hasn't been able to add the finishing touch. Roglič has little in the way of climbing support outside of young Australian Luke Tuckwell, and Mas too doesn't have domestiques working for him on the level of Gregor Mühlberger, and Gall has already shown that Decathlon aren't going to go down without a serious fight. "I think Decathlon's still gonna try something, I'm sure. Also, even if it's just for a stage win or to win some time again towards Mas and Primož and also Oscar Onley. So it will be interesting," said Vanthourenhout. "Also, Mas, I think he's still going to fight for some more seconds and a bigger time gap than he has now. He also knows that even if it is still a nice 1:00 to 1:30 advantage on his contenders, it's still not enough to win the Vuelta. So for sure he's also going to try it now in that second week to take some seconds or do some moves, but we have our plan and made that clear on the rest day."While the most famous moment of his career has been letting the 2020 Tour slip away in the final time trial to Pogačar, Roglič has also chased down riders in the final week to win Grand Tours in the past, even as recently as Ben O'Connor in 2024, when he didn't go into the red until stage 19.But at 36 and with crashes and injuries continuing to hamper him from having ideal preparation for his biggest goals, has Roglič still got it in him to claim a fifth Vuelta a España title, and stand alone as the record holder?All may become clear on stage 12's last two climbs, the Alto de Velefique and the final ascent to Calar Alto.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Who will join the Yankees’ Circle of Trust?
item.author: Jake Devin
item.content:encoded: Of all the Yankees moves (or non-moves) this summer, their decision not to add pitching at the trade deadline probably caused the most consternation. The team’s pitching staff paced the league in the first half, sure, but most fans looked at the club’s bullpen, and at the long list of names on the IL, and figured the Yankees could use an extra arm or two just in case, just to add a little depth if things got hairy.Well, we’re here in September, and things have gotten hairy, but the Yankees’ pitching staff has still performed. Max Fried and Ryan Weathers hit the IL with an elbow issues, and Fernando Cruz’s injury left the late-inning crew thin, and yet the Yankees’ team ERA of 2.77 since August 4th leads baseball. Their depth has been tested, and they’ve aced the test.All that said, outside of David Bednar, Brent Headrick, and Paul Blackburn, there’s no obvious pecking order in the Yankee bullpen. Aaron Boone has three clear favorite options, and then a bunch of question marks. Other than the matter of how to structure the team’s outfield, this might be the most pressing roster concern to sort out in the final month. So, who will emerge as the next most trustworthy reliever in Boone’s bullpen?I think the most fun part of this question is that the answer could be anyone, thanks to the Yankees’ proclivity for getting the best out of unheralded pitchers. Anyone that is currently on the roster, or working on things in Triple-A, or rehabbing from injury, is liable to step in and surprise us, because Matt Blake and his staff have been so proficient at molding flawed pitchers into serious contributors.That leaves us with loads of possible players who could emerge in September to establish themselves in the Circle of Trust before the playoffs begin. We could start with the young big leaguers coming back from injuries, Luis Gil, Clarke Schmidt, and Ryan Weathers. Gil, who missed most of this year with a shoulder problem, has returned as a reliever and looked intriguing, sitting 96 mph with his fastball in an outing on Monday night and generating six whiffs. Schmidt is coming off a longer layoff post Tommy John surgery, but also has a high-quality track record; his 3.07 ERA across 2024 and 2025 speaks to how effective he can be when healthy. Weathers morphed into one of the best starters in baseball after a midseason repertoire shift, and could be a dynamite bullpen weapon if he can make it back healthy. It wouldn’t be a surprise to see any of this trio become a key bullpen figure by the end of the month.Then, there are the late-season scrap heap finds that the Yankees are actively working on. Last week, they dusted off Michael Fulmer, best known around here for swiping the 2016 Rookie of the Year award from Gary Sanchez, and also claimed John Schreiber off waivers. Fulmer has made three appearances with New York and flashed a somewhat interesting cutter-led arsenal, while Schreiber tossed a scoreless inning his Yankees debut Tuesday night and was a dependable middle reliever as recently as last year. It’s entirely possible both with will be off the roster before long, but would you be shocked if one of them benefited from working with Blake and proved they had something left in the tank?From there, we have the arms in the minors that might seem like long shots, but have performed in the bigs before. The most interesting name is probably Angel Chivilli, who used a sharp changeup to dominate through the month of July before a six-run blowup against the Cardinals in early August ruined his season numbers. The Yankees also have Yerry De los Santos and Brendan Beck as possible options in Scranton. No, no ones wants the Yankees to be relying on these kinds of guys in October, and it’s unlikely any emerge as real options, but it’s not out of the realm of possibility they return to the bigs in September and show something. Elmer Rodríguez could’ve fit with this group of minors options, but he’s back with the big-league squad, and he too merits mention as someone that could earn Boone’s faith with a strong showing this month. The fact of the matter is, the Yankees have some unsettled spots in the bullpen, and one month to decide who should fill them. Who do you think will step up? Will one or more of these guys find themselves adding to the Circle of Trust?The Yankees are off today, getting some time to make the short jaunt down from Anaheim to San Diego. There will be plenty on the site to keep you busy, as Sam runs down the Yankees Plays of August, and Peter recaps Wednesday’s American League action. Later, Jonathan profiles Eric Plunk, the only player ever traded for the same Hall of Famer twice, while Andrés discusses Clarke Schmidt’s impending addition to the Yankee bullpen, and the rapid ascent of Yankee prospect Yostin Pena.

item.title: 'It's changed a lot' – Paul Seixas raring to take on Canadian GPs and World Championships with Pogačar's possible absence opening up opportunities
item.content:encoded: Fresh off of fourth in his debut Tour de France, Paul Seixas is highly motivated to take on his final block of racing in 2026 – and perhaps even more of a contender with Tadej Pogačar's participation in the coming races in doubt.First up, though, is a first-ever trip to North America for the Grand Prixs de Québec and Montréal next week, which will not only be a good warm-up for the Worlds in Montréal, but could be a good chance for Seixas to score a win, too."It's a really good opportunity for me," Seixas told assembled media on Wednesday, speaking from an altitude in Les Arcs where he is preparing for his final goals of 2026. "I think obviously the course that suits me more in the Montreal Grand Prix, because I think it's a bit harder than Québec. I look at the races last year, and Québec was really more open for a lot of riders, and Montréal was really hard from what I heard and from what I saw. It was really hard pace and of course the positioning is really important, but you see, in the end, it was really by the pedal stroke, and by the strength in the legs, more than in Québec. But I think both races are open, also because now it's different without Pogačar, so we will see."The chance to check out the Worlds course in advance is also obviously a big draw for the Frenchman, who finished 13th in the road race in Kigali last year and will be hoping for a lot better this year."To race two weeks before on the same course as Worlds is really important, and I can really see points where I have to improve my tactics, and how it feels to be in the bunch and how are the roads."Straight back to work after the TourFinishing fourth overall in the Tour de France in only his second year as a pro – at still only 19 – Seixas' season is undoubtedly already a huge success, but he certainly didn't take the foot off the gas after the Tour and has a lot of motivation for these final big goals.Far from being fatigued after a busy season, Seixas seems to be feeling better than ever."I did time off after the Tour, and I think that was really good, really well managed by the team, so I feel fresh now," he explained. "We are in a training camp at altitude in Les Arcs. I'm really happy for what I did after the Tour, I think it was good. I can build on some good base after the Tour and all the season."I feel great, honestly, on the bike. So I think I'm ready to be good in the last block of races for the end of the season. Of course, the main goals remain the World Championships and Lombardia, so I think I can build strength day by day from now on."This may be his first time kicking off his late-season goals with the Canadian races, but Seixas knows from last year what it takes to put together a good final block, and given his success last autumn, he seems to have an 'if it isn't broken, don't fix it' mentality. Despite being a year – and a Grand Tour – further into his career, he's not in a drastically different place in terms of confidence or feeling than he was during his break-out autumn 12 months ago."I think I'm pretty much at the same point," he said. "Last year when I came here, it was different because I had Tour de l'Avenir before, so I wasn't feeling the best at this moment last year. This year I'm coming from two weeks of training, so it's different. But I feel ready, in the end. I feel good in my head, I feel ready mentally, and I think physically I'm already quite good. So I think I will be good, I hope. I feel ready."The big difference between this year and last year, though, is that Seixas might not be up against Tadej Pogačar this time around.Pogačar was never due to do the Canadian races, opting for the Vuelta a España instead to build up to Worlds and Lombardia, but his heavy crash out of the Spanish race and subsequent surgery have placed question marks over whether he can even be back in action for his final goals of 2026."Of course, I think it's changed a lot," Seixas said of Pogačar's crash and possible race absences. "First, I want to say that I think it was really unlucky for him. We all saw the video, and what happened was really unlucky. It can happen to anyone. "Now, of course, it changes the racing because, as we see from this year and the past years, he is really the boss of cycling, so when he is here, he changes the race on his own. But now it will be maybe a bit more open. But there is a lot of strong riders still, and I guess we'll see. "It will be interesting to see how it goes in Montréal, and maybe after that we can have a look at what can happen in Worlds."He was also not afraid to admit that Pogačar's absence does change his mindset going into these races, although he wasn't getting ahead of himself or ruling out a return for the Slovenian. "Honestly, I think that it changes a lot in the head," he said. "Because when Tadej is here, you have to think about how you're going to race with him, so it's pretty much like you see when he attacks you just try to hang on, and if you attack before – you can try something, of course, but there's really not much chance that it succeeds because he has a strong team. When he feels like he's in danger, he can do anything."But for the moment, it's too soon to think about it. We only learned about the crash a few days before, and we don't know how it goes for him. So I hope he can recover as fast as he can."Whether Pogačar makes it back or not, though, Seixas will still be up against some hugely strong riders in Canada these next few weeks, and rather than being cowed by the strength of the field, he's raring to go.He'll face the likes of Remco Evenepoel and Tom Pidcock already in the Grand Prixs, and then added horsepower from Wout van Aert and Mathieu van der Poel for Worlds."I'm really excited," he said about racing against Van der Poel specifically, a rider he hasn't faced often in one-day races. "He's a great rider that I watch for more than five years on TV, and it's really a dream to compete against him and against Remco and the others. And I'm really motivated to look forward to battle with them."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: NBA investigation ends with LA Clippers sent 25 seasons back in time
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: The NBA’s nearly year-long investigation into the Los Angeles Clippers has ended with one of the harshest punishments in league history, sending the franchise back to territory last seen during Minnesota’s Joe Smith salary-cap scandal 25 seasons ago.The League has concluded that the Clippers violated salary-cap circumvention rules by facilitating endorsement deals for Kawhi Leonard with Aspiration, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics and Lockton Insurance, as first reported by ESPN’s Shams Charania.The investigation began after reporting by Torre, and the process was conducted by Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.The sanctions immediately reshape the Clippers’ already-long-gone future:The Clippers have been fined $30 million, the largest team fine in NBA history.Los Angeles is losing its first-round picks in 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033.The Clippers have been placed under a five-year compliance and monitoring program.Owner Steve Ballmer has been suspended from all league and team activities for one year.President of business operations Gillian Zucker has been suspended without pay for one year.President of basketball operations Lawrence Frank has been suspended without pay for six months.Leonard was fined $700,000 for improper benefits.Dennis “Uncle Dennis” Robertson has been banned from conducting business with NBA teams for five years, although Kawhi is his lone client.The scale of the punishment closely mirrors, although it clearly tops it, the NBA’s response to Minnesota in 2000. More than 25 years ago, former NBA commissioner David Stern stripped the Timberwolves of five first-round picks and fined the franchise $3.5 million after determining it had entered into an illegal secret agreement with Smith. Two of Minnesota’s five picks were later returned.The Clippers’ draft situation is particularly tough. After years of outgoing picks tied to the Paul George trade, the latest penalties leave Los Angeles of its own first-round selections under the current setup. Sheesh…The NBA suspended Ballmer for knowingly seeking to help Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities and approving a business arrangement connected to the Aspiration endorsement. Zucker was cited for being directly culpable in the endorsement arrangements and for providing false and misleading statements to investigators, while Frank was disciplined for his involvement and for approving impermissible expenses involving Leonard and his family.Funnily enough, Leonard’s punishment differed significantly from Smith’s 25 seasons earlier, as Kawhi came out pretty much unscathed. Smith’s contract was voided in 2000, while the NBA decided to leave Leonard’s contract intact and instead ordered him to pay $700,000 over improper benefits. Lots of money to us, pocket money for the Klaw.Los Angeles “vehemently” rejected the NBA’s findings and said it intends to challenge the ruling through every available avenue. Meanwhile, Kawhi is still on his way to Canada to play basketball north of the border next season.

item.title: Yankees news: Cole opines on Angels sale
item.author: Kento Mizuno
item.content:encoded: New York Daily News | Gary Phillips: Gerrit Cole grew up an Angels fan, so it’s only natural that he would have something to say about the franchise’s recent sale to Kroenke Sports & Entertainment. However, the veteran approached the issue from a business standpoint rather than an emotional one, noting that the club’s ultimate price tag of $4 billion was remarkably high, especially when compared to the Padres, who were sold for $3.9 billion earlier this year despite being much more competitive in recent years. Said Cole: “It shows that there’s ability to get top dollar on both ends of the spectrum…I think that would speak to how healthy economically the game is functioning.” Definitely something to keep in mind as the MLBPA and the owners continue their standoff. NJ.com | Randy Miller: With rosters having expanded on September 1st, the Yankees’ additions were 3B Ryan McMahon and reliever John Schreiber. Here, Miller liaises with an anonymous scout who shares his evaluations on several players who were passed over, including pitching prospect and 2026 debutant Brendan Beck, and former regulars Anthony Volpe and Jasson Dominguez. The scout doesn’t really tell us anything new about the latter two, but his comments on Beck are interesting; he pegs him as a fifth starter and a trade chip of some value despite his relatively advanced age. Not bad for a guy who was drafted 55th overall, then had Tommy John surgery just six months after. The Athletic | Asli Petit: In a first for MLB, the Yankees now have an official tampon! Sequel, an upstart company founded by two women ex-athletes, has partnered with the club to offer free tampons in Yankee Stadium’s women’s bathrooms. I wouldn’t have guessed that the Yankees of all teams would be the first team to embark on such a partnership, but it’s a welcome change and an important step towards ensuring the inclusion of female fans. Hopefully more clubs will follow suit!ESPN.com: The Yankees have struggled to close the gap between them and the Rays in the division race (though it’s certainly closer now than it once was). It’s still a long shot, but the Yankees have one thing going for them; the remaining strength of schedule. The Yankees’ upcoming opponents have a collective winning percentage of .489, markedly lower than the Rays’ slate of .517. The two teams are set to face off in the penultimate series of the season. Here’s hoping the Yankees can handle their business against their lackluster opponents leading up to that all-too-important matchup.A couple of tweets to round out today’s roundup: first, a quick overview of how Spencer Jones has produced since his second call-up. I have never been more happy to eat crow, and I hope Jones forces me to continue my raven-based diet. Second, Clarke Schmidt inches nearer to his return, as he’s been reassigned from Double-A to Triple-A for his rehab. With the Yankees piggybacking Max Fried and Will Warren on Friday, it’s fair to wonder if Schmidt could also be a piggyback candidate should he rejoin the big league club according to schedule.

item.title: Next-Gen Radar: Tour de l'Avenir, junior talents, and all the under-23 action from August
item.content:encoded: Hello and welcome to the first in a new series for our monthly under-23 racing wrap-up!As the pros get younger and younger and talent spotting gets more and more important for WorldTour teams, under-23 and even junior racing is more important than ever, so we wanted to start giving you a monthly overview of all the main stories, riders and races.We'll mainly focus on road racing, and mainly the under-23 categories, but we'll throw in some junior races and some off-road stories too – multidisciplinary stars are the future, after all, and the junior ranks are the new under-23 when it comes to talent spotting. We will include a revolving mix of sections, including obviously all the main results and transfers, but also dedicated sections on riders from Australia, New Zealand, North and South America and around the world, calling on expertise from our Australian and North American Editors.We'd also love to know what you'd like to see in this round-up. Rider Q&As? Agent insights? More analysis? Let me know in the comments below; I'd love to hear your thoughts.For now, though, let's get into all the main stories and action from August.The biggest under-23 race in August was undoubtedly the Tour de l'Avenir, the long-standing race touted as the mini Tour de France and indeed often a very strong indicator of who will do well in the professional Grand Tours. This year's edition was a little bit different, as for the first time the event was raced primarily in trade development teams rather than national squads, which arguably made for a more professionalised dynamic.Unfortunately, there was no women's race this year, after the organisers scrapped the race for 2026 citing costs and lack of development teams. They say they want to replace it with a women's junior race, but no word on that yet.Lorenzo Finn (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) 21:56:50Niels Driesen (Lotto-Groupe Wanty) +2:34Matteo Vanhuffel (Picnic PostNL Development) +3:42So, for the racing we did get: 23-year-old world champion and Giro d'Italia Next Gen winner Lorenzo Finn (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe Rookies) went into the race as a huge favourite and duly delivered, winning the TT and the final road stage to secure the GC with a 2:34 gap.Niels Driesen (Lotto-Groupe Wanty) finished second, with Picnic PostNL Development rider Matteo Vanhuffel third. The other stage winners were Driesen, Keije Solen (Lotto-Groupe Wanty), Davide Stella (UAE Team Emirates Gen Z), Kasper Borremans (Bahrain Victorious Development Team), and a name you probably already know, Aubin Sparfel (Decathlon CMA CGM Development Team). I couldn't have finished this Tour de l'Avenir any better. I’m really grateful to the team. We went all in for the stage win today. The final climb was very hard and I’m super happy that I managed to finish it off. Together with the Giro Next Gen, the Tour de l’Avenir was my big goal this year, and I’ve won both. That makes me very proud.The most interesting thing about the race was perhaps that it actually wasn't that surprising at all, and I think this comes down to the change to trade teams. With national teams, such a diverse range of riders got a chance to ride l'Avenir, and there were chances for riders to announce themselves there. Now, with the proliferation of development teams and indeed the growing professionalisation of the under-23 level, l'Avenir is less a career-launching race and more a career-confirming one. Every stage winner this year, and indeed last year, was on a WorldTour development squad, and most already have their spot in the WorldTour secured for 2027. This is no longer the race to spot talent at – if riders are winning here, they've already proved themselves well before the Tour de l'Avenir.All that said, it is still a really good and important race, and Finn's victory just confirms even more what a talent he is, and that he will be a force to be reckoned with when he steps up to Red Bull's WorldTour programme in January.(Ineos Grenadiers Racing Academy) won the Gran Premio Sportivi di Poggiana - Trofeo Bonin Costruzioni (1.2U)(Bahrain Victorious Development Team) won the GP Capodarco Comunita di Capodarco (1.2U)(Kasper crypto4me) won the West Bohemia Tour (2.2U)But make no mistake, this isn't just an off-road story – Wright is a huge road talent, too. After winning the final stage of the Tour of Tasmania, he's been racing in Europe since April, partly for the Australian national squad and partly for a Dutch club team, and he's secured wins in France and Slovakia, plus third overall at the Junioren Rundfahrt.He's off to Tudor Pro Cycling's under-23 development squad for 2027, so his talent has definitely been spotted, and he should be on your radar, too.Long-term, I aim to represent Australia at the 2028 Olympic Games and build a career on the road. I thrive in hard road races as a punchier rider, though and for now, I still have work to do on the long climbs.Australian riders had a pretty low-key Tour de l'Avenir – there were no New Zealand starters – with the best performer, 12th twice and 38th overall for Lidl-Trek Future Racing. Nations like Australia and New Zealand are definitely among the more heavily affected by the move to trade teams, which naturally favour more European riders and mean we'll see fewer riders from nations like these in the race. It places much more pressure on these riders to get spots on trade teams, and takes away the chance to race via their national federation, which is unfortunate to see.The big question going forward regarding New Zealand is whether we're going to see any under-23 or junior riders at the World Championships. Riders often get fairly minimal support from Cycling New Zealand, often having to self-fund at least part of their trip, so participation is sometimes low. and were the only under-23 representatives, men or women, to race in Kigali, with Pringle scoring silver in the TT, so he'll be hopeful of racing in Montreal. Connolly could also be a good shout as he has been racing in the US this summer.The best-performing riders from North and South America in Tour de l'Avenir were (UAE Team Emirates Gen Z) in fourth and (Soudal Quick-Step Devo) in fifth. For Ramírez, fourth may have felt like a bit of a disappointment given he was second at the Giro Next Gen, and perhaps similar for Bravo as he won the Giro delle Valle d'Aosta and came third at the Giro Next Gen.However, both results were really big ones, especially for Bravo from a really under-represented cycling nation in Brazil. He's been impressing all season, and will surely be flying the Brazilian flag in the WorldTour peloton soon, though Pinarello-Q36.5 are interested in his signature, too. We interviewed him earlier this year if you want to find out more about him.It’s a new world of experience, and it was basically a school; I learned every day – how to position, to race as a team - and basically everything that in Brazil you don’t have.Over in North America, the highlight of August was definitely the return of the Philadelphia Cycling Classic, where under-23 riders from teams like Meridian Racing p/b de la Uz, Competitive Edge Racing and Virginia's Blue Ridge-TWENTY28 got to rub shoulders with WorldTour riders. 20-year-old hugely impressed with third in the women's race, a result which – paired with her solid ride for Team USA at the Tour de Pologne – surely will have put her on some big teams' radars.Here are some of the most notable under-23 transfers you should know about this month:Héctor Alvarez → Lidl-Trek (development team graduate)Seth Dunwoody → Bahrain Victorious (development team graduate)Gavin Sherry → EF Education-EasyPost (development team graduate)There are a couple of road races coming up on the men's under-23 circuit – the Giro della Regione Friuli Venezia Giulia stage race kicks off on Thursday, and the Flanders Tomorrow Tour on Friday – but the main focus now will be on the Road World Championships and the age category road races and TTs in Montréal.Because he's still only 19, will be a pretty big favourite to repeat his title in the under-23 men's road race, and possibly the time trial as well, although the race against the clock is likely a lot more open. Fresh off of eighth overall in the Tour de France Femmes, home favourite will be aiming big in the women's under-23 events, and could bring home a big win – or two – for Canada.We'll have full previews of the contenders for the under-23 and junior races throughout the World Championships, plus news and interviews from our team on the ground, so stick around for more under-23 coverage in September.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!

item.title: F1's take on its battle to satisfy new and old fans
item.author: Jon Noble
item.content:encoded: Bernie Ecclestone once infamously said that there was little point in Formula 1 chasing a younger audience, because they could not afford what sponsors had on offer.Now, well into the post-Ecclestone Liberty Media era, F1 not only has a bigger audience but a much younger one, too.The latest figures issued by F1 suggest that 830 million people now follow grand prix racing, which is 64% up from 2018 when its current owner took over.It is estimated that 43% of F1's audience is now under 35, with 42% of the audience female. Out of the new fans, three quarters are female.While the numbers are a huge triumph for Liberty, they are also at the heart of a debate triggered by the divided opinion over the 2026 rules.How much should F1 and its stakeholders obsess over the new audience, and what should you do about the fans who have long been there?Turn off the hardcore, who will stick with you through thick and thin, then there may be nobody left if the bubble bursts and the casuals are lost, too.Those notorious Ecclestone remarks about younger fans came just as F1 began its hybrid era back in 2014."Young kids will see the Rolex brand, but are they going to go and buy one?" he said back then. "They can't afford it. Or our other sponsor, UBS - these kids don't care about banking. They haven't got enough money to put in the bloody banks anyway. That's what I think."F1 is in a very different place right now, thanks to the new approach taken by Liberty.According to FOM's chief communications and corporate relations officer Liam Parker, this wasn't an Americanisation of F1."It was a modernisation approach," he told The Race.There was a time in the 1980s when all F1 had to really care about was making sure it was in front of as many TV eyeballs as possible on Sunday afternoons.Ecclestone's approach to maximise the audience and the value for broadcast deals was to lock down the distribution of content to increase its exclusivity.His successors – then-CEO Chase Carey and commercial chief Sean Bratches – viewed things differently. Rather than shut off everything on social media and view it as the enemy, they embraced it and saw opportunity.Parker says: "Their view was, 'well, look, we've got access to all of this. How can we cut this in different ways?'."'Why don't we have a social media team that is large enough to service a wider audience? Why are the teams not allowed to post content? Why are the drivers not allowed?'"It was this mindset that opened the doors for a different approach through social media and paved the way for the Netflix: Drive to Survive show that had a major role in delivering a new audience.While Drive to Survive was important in attracting a new F1 audience, it should not be viewed as the magic bullet that did it all. Instead, it more amplified F1's new Liberty Media approach.Parker adds: "A lot of credit is given to Netflix about what it did, and it deserves it, but it wasn't the panacea."I genuinely believe the opening up of social media access, alongside the Netflix environment, that then built into the F1 film and other things, shifted the demographic quite substantially. That's taken time."What a new audience meansWhen audiences and customers change, organisations must react.There is always a balancing act required in responding to what your new followers want without it risking being a turn-off for those who have been around a while.In F1's case, it has been able to satisfy different segments quite easily off track by simply expanding the content on offer.There are those happy to follow F1 simply through watching 15-second TikTok videos, while those that want technical analyses that pore over the finest of details can find that, too. One offering does not come at the expense of the other.As Parker says: "If you just rely on, ‘let's just put out racing content', you're serving a certain market and hoping that the new market will just like that."You've got to keep up with trends. You've got to work out where the trends are."There's no point saying, ‘OK, we've got a growing fanbase aged between 16 and 20,' without saying, ‘well, what do they consume? How do they get their information? How do they get their entertainment? What news do they consume? What are they interested in and what are they not interested in?'"It is here where F1 faces a bit of a juggling act because different audiences value different content in different ways.For some, Lewis Hamilton's latest clothing choice is as important as the latest rear wing design is to others."If you talk about tyres and degradation in a video, then there's a whole load of people that just don't understand it," adds Parker. "They perhaps feel stupid and then don't want to be a part of it."They just want to know that Charles Leclerc turned up with the dog today. How big is George Russell's fiancée's wedding ring?"That is just different content. What we shouldn't say is 'this [bit of content is] trivial, and that bit is far more serious'."The hardcore vs casual debateVarying needs of different audience segments go beyond just content though, because the make-up of the fanbase inevitably feeds through to what shape F1 itself should take.When it comes to deciding rule changes, a key factor is always whether fans will like them or they'll prove to be a turn-off. And you are never going to please all the fans all the time.There are times when a series has to decide whether it moulds itself into becoming what its fanbase wants, or if it commits to doing what it thinks is best and expects the audience to adapt.This is something that F1 has faced head-on in 2026 with the new regulations having clearly divided opinion between audience segments.Some have embraced the action-packed overtakes that many F1 drivers and hardcore fans have bemoaned as fake. Many could also not care less about the cars being energy-starved and how super-clipping has ruined some great corners.F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali recently caused some controversy as he upset established and new fans alike in response to a question about the more hardcore of followers not liking the new rules."There are diehard motorsport fans who talk about clipping during a Formula 1 weekend," he told De Telegraaf. "But there will also be many who think of a clip as something you put in your hair."Coming off the back of a comment he made over the summer that "no one is interested in how you drive the car", Domenicali's stance has left many long-term fans questioning whether they are now just a minority that F1 no longer cares about.Parker is clear that is not the case - and he suggests Domenicali's hair clip remark was misinterpreted."I was in the room, and Stefano wasn't dismissive," he said. "He explained that he was a super fan, but he also had to think about those that are not."There's a great set of people out there that are our core, that care about clipping and battery state and charge, and you must give them that content."But there's others out there that think a clip is what you put in your hair. He wasn't saying that no one cares about super clipping. It's just different content ignites different people in different debates."Not messing with the rulesParker is adamant that while F1 has not hesitated to rip things up when it comes to content, there is a red line that it will not cross.It is that grand prix racing must remain a meritocracy where the best drivers in the best cars come out on top. The sport will always come before the entertainment."The sport is the core," he said. "You can't mess with that."Parker says evidence of this being central to Liberty's remit is that, while it's not afraid to shake up the experience for fans at grand prix weekends, the on-track elements have not been radically overhauled."I bet if you went back 10 years and asked someone to crystal ball gaze and say, ‘what do you think Liberty as an American company would do to F1', you'd say 'they will probably have sprinklers and have fake this and fake that'," he said."I think the most ambitious thing we've really done on track is to evolve the sprint races over time."For F1, delivering a quality spectacle that stays true to its roots is something that is good for all fans."If that's strong, then everything else has a strong basis," added Parker."If people are saying that racing is rubbish, the drivers are boring, there's no entertainment, these cars are not interesting, then there isn't a Netflix story, there isn't a social media story."But he says that F1 must be mindful that it cannot stay locked in the past. It has to evolve and adapt to ensure that there is a new generation of fans coming through, otherwise global interest will fall away."If F1 works and is fundamentally strong, then everything else goes from it," he said."There are fans that have been with us a long time, and they are vital. Hopefully they will be with us all the way through."But we would be wrong to say that, as a sport, all these other people that don't understand the technology, 'we don't want you'. From a sporting perspective and potentially a commercial perspective it would be stupid."I know sometimes it gets lost in understanding, but Stefano has been in the sport for 30 years, it's his business, but he's got to think: 'How do I make it bigger? How do I grow?'"Because if you sit still, the NBA, cricket, football, everything else will grow, and we'll be left behind."Sitting still is not something you'd associate with the Liberty F1 era, but keeping that much more varied audience – rather than winning it over in the first place – could be its greatest challenge yet.

item.title: Tadej Pogačar out of hospital after Vuelta a España crash and injuries but questions remain regarding World Championships
item.content:encoded: In images posted to social media by his partner, Urška Žigart, Pogačar can be seen standing outside next to personal friend and UAE team soigneur Žiga Jerman. with his left arm in sling. Jerman is a personal friend and soigneur with the UAE team, who has accompanied Pogačar since he crashed on stage 8 of the Vuelta whilst leading the race.Whilst Pogačar's return home marks a major step forward in his recovery, the next question of when he will next race is still uncertain.The original plans for the Slovenian star were that following La Vuelta a España, he would take part in the World Championships on September 27 to try for a record-equalling third rainbow title. After that, he would then head to the European Championships on October 4, followed by his usual season-closing race at Il Lombardia on October 10.All of these races technically remain on the calendar, and even if comments by the Slovenian national team doctor, Krištof Knap, reported by Slovenian state TV channel were anything but optimistic regarding their feasibility, the possibility of Pogačar being there is not completely ruled out.Asked if Pogačar could be racing within a month, despite his injuries, Knap stated: "It's not realistic, even though we all would like it.""In the end, Tadej Pogačar is also a man who has to live the rest of his life in his own body after the end of his career. It's good that he won't continue to suffer any consequences."After all, he still has a few years of his career ahead of him and it's important that he completes full rehabilitation without rushing."Members of Pogačar's trade team, UAE, have been much less categorical about the chances that he won't race the Worlds, whilst both riders and management have emphasised that the top priority is his recovery."I also think it will be difficult to be fit for the World Championships," Domen Novak said to "But Tadej is a hard worker. He never gives up and he is trying to recover quickly.”According to, Pogačar will make his definitive decision about where and when he will next compete on Friday, although this has yet to be confirmed. But if it is to be in an event this autumn, Pogačar's race against time has already begun.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Yankees secure series in extras thanks to clutch Wells, dominant Schlittler
item.author: Peter Brody
item.content:encoded: How good has Austin Wells been of late? Initially starting this game on the bench, Wells joined the action in the eighth with a pinch-hit single to prime his bat for the true decisive blow — the go-ahead two-out, two-run single in the tenth to salvage a win from a day when it looked like the offense would squander another brilliant Cam Schlittler start. Schlittler’s velocity was down about a tick-and-a-half from his amped up last start against the Red Sox, but that didn’t sap any of his effectiveness. After walking a career-high five batters his last time out (albeit across 5.2 scoreless against Boston), there seemed to be a concerted effort to really attack the zone. This led to quick outs on a lot of early contact in the opening innings before he honed his command to the edges, leading to an uptick in strikeouts toward the end of his outing. He got three straight groundouts in the third and then navigated around a Vaughn Grissom single to leadoff the second by striking out Moisés Ballesteros on a pair of overpowering fastballs. The third and fourth brought another strikeout each, Schlittler remaining economical with his pitch count in both frames. The fifth saw him shift into high gear as he was able to gas a pair of four-seamers by Ballesteros and Christian Moore for his fifth and sixth strikeouts.Schlittler needed to be shutdown given the way the offense struggled against Reid Detmers. Widely expected to get traded at the deadline, the Angels hung on to their starter and he rewarded them with a 1.55 ERA in eight starts since the break. The bats had no answer the first time through the order, Detmers needing just 30 pitches to make it through three perfect innings. The script flipped upon facing him for the second time, Paul Goldschmidt and Cody Bellinger opening the fourth with a pair of singles. Heliot Ramos couldn’t follow suit, grounding into what is already his fifth double play in 76 plate appearances for the Yankees. However, Ben Rice kept the inning alive with a two-out infield single, allowing Amed Rosario to open the scoring with an RBI ground-rule double that one-hopped the fence in right. However, you couldn’t help but feel they left meat on the bone between the Ramos GIDP and Spencer Jones striking out to strand Rice at third.There was a scary moment in the sixth when a Rice foul line drive struck a camera man in the head near the Yankees’ dugout, and it was relieving to see him get up under his own power and get carted off after an over ten minute delay. To Detmers’ credit, he settled down after the fourth, retiring ten of the final 11 batters he faced to end his outing with seven innings of one-run ball.Schlittler kept cruising through the sixth, punching out Oswald Peraza on a gross curveball and Travis D’Arnaus looking on a painted heater. He got two outs into the seventh to make it 17 retired in a row before making his lone mistake of the outing, and unfortunately for him it left the yard, Grissom crushing a center-cut cutter to dead center just over the outstretched glove of Jones at the wall. His pitch count was only at 83, so it was a no-brainer to send Schlittler back out for the eighth. He retired the side in order to complete eight innings for the third time this season. It was also his fifth straight start giving up one or fewer runs, and 19th such start overall on the year to set a new franchise record. He had all his pitches working, it’s just a shame the one mistake he made got punished on a night when his offense couldn’t hold up their end of the bargain. He ended his outing having given up a run on two hits and no walks with nine strikeouts in eight innings.David Bednar was tasked with pitching a scoreless ninth to give his offense a chance in extra innings, and he did so with aplomb, striking out three to nullify a Mike Trout single. Off to extras this game went, the Yankees loading the bases with one out on a José Caballero single and Jazz Chisholm Jr. walk. A Luis García Jr. infield fly put them on the brink of wasting the opportunity, but it also brought one of their most clutch hitters of late to the plate in Wells.Wells fouled off three straight elevated heaters before getting one he could handle, grounding a single just past the dive attempts of the first and second basemen to plate a pair and take the lead. That opened the floodgates against reliever Luke Murphy, who gave up three straight singles to Bellinger, Trent Grisham, and Rice, each one plating an additional run to make it 6-1 in favor of the Yankees by the time Rosario flew out to end the frame.Recent bullpen signing Michael Fulmer was entrusted to record the final three outs, and he certainly made us sweat a little. He gave up a two-run blast to Ballesteros, but bounced back to retire the next two batters and nail down the victory, 6-3.That is what you are supposed to do against the worst team in baseball. Stay in the game long enough until you expose their fatal flaw — in this case, LA’s bullpen — and then capitalize on the opportunities you create for yourself. It’s the Yankees’ fourth series win out of their last five as they become the second team in the AL to reach 80 wins and draw within 3.5 games of the Rays after they lost to the Mets earlier in the day.The Yankees get tomorrow off before making the short journey to San Diego for three games. Max Fried is scheduled to make his second start back from his latest IL stint facing Walker Buehler in the opener Friday night. First pitch is scheduled for 9:40 p.m. ET with the broadcast remaining on YES.

item.title: Tiffany Cromwell to say goodbye to racing career at home UCI Gravel World Championships in October
item.author: simone.giuliani@futurenet.com (Simone Giuliani)
item.content:encoded: Tiffany Cromwell has announced that her 18-year career as a professional racer on the road is now over, and she will deliver her final goodbye off-road, at the UCI Gravel World Championships in Western Australia on October 10.The South Australian has long been one of the nation's key figures in the peloton, starting out with the Lotto Ladies Team in 2010, moving to Hitec Products and then Orica-AIS before settling in at the squad now known as Canyon-SRAM. The rider who has represented Australia at the Olympic Games and World Championships has a win tally on the road that includes Omloop Het Nieuwsblad and two stages of the Giro d'Italia, but her role more recently has been focussed on helping her teammates chase victory, with the experienced 38-year-old often slotting in as road captain."I’ve been fortunate to have had a very long cycling career with only one major injury," said Cromwell in a social media post announcing her retirement. "I’ve also been able to experience and be a part of the massive change and growth of women’s cycling. "There’s been many highs and lows and many amazing memories. And I’m happy to be able to finish on my own terms."Cromwell had initially planned to retire at the end of the 2022 season, having thought she would bow out with a home World Championships on the road in Wollongong. However, the rider, who had now also incorporated gravel into her schedule, decided back then she wasn't yet ready to walk away. After another four years in the peloton, she instead took her final bow on the road in the United States, having outlined that the Philadelphia Cycling Classic had been her last road race."Philly was a great race to be able to close out this chapter of my career. An iconic race with so much history that was back for the first time in 10 years. The atmosphere was electric, and as an added bonus, we managed to take home the victory as a team with Chiara Consonni," said Cromwell, adding that there were still three gravel races to go, and the last of those is where she'll get her home-nation farewell.Cromwell has found considerable success in gravel, with a win tally that includes a list of UCI Gravel World Series races and two Unbound 100 wins, plus she has swept up the national title in the discipline over the last two years. That makes this year's Gravel World Championships in Nannup a fitting farewell as she will bow out as the reigning national champion in a home World Championships race, which also happens to be on the same course where she celebrated victory at the SEVEN UCI Gravel World Series race earlier this year.A victory there again would, of course, make for the perfect fairytale ending, but no matter where she finishes, she'll be guaranteed one of the loudest cheers of the weekend's racing.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews.
